$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-14\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-15\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\,+$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}(2t-1){e}^{-2t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}(2t-1){e}^{-2t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2(0)} \\ {e}^{-2(0)}\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}(2\cdot 0-1){e}^{-2(0)} \\ 0\cdot {e}^{-2(0)}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0) \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0)\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+1 \\ {c}_{1}+3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+1=-1 \\ {c}_{1}+3=6\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${c}_{1}=3.$  Substituting this into the second equation and solving for ${c}_{2},$ we get ${c}_{2}=8.$ 

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=3\cdot [\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}(2t+1){e}^{-2t} \\ (t+1){e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].
$$
